tasks.task: Rank open invoices into a chase plan

items.when: When you have an aged debt report or open invoice list and need who to chase first and how
When the list is chased every week, to get who to chase, a reminder each and a 90-day cash view
When you want days outstanding and where cash is stuck across debtors, creditors and stock
When one big customer pays late, to map the risk and set a limit before you push

tasks.task: Write reminder messages from friendly to firm

items.when: When each stage needs a short message with the amount, the date and how to pay
When each customer needs a gentle or a firm version to choose between
When you know the history with one customer and the reminder should start where they are
When one late invoice matters and you want a warm reminder, then a firm follow-up
When the debtor is a UK business, to add statutory interest and the fixed fee correctly
When the facts are right but the tone is off, to rewrite it warmer or firmer
When a customer has gone quiet, to open with their side and ask a calm question

tasks.task: Check supplier invoices before they are approved or paid

items.when: When a batch of bills is due for approval and each needs totals, tax and details checked
When you have the files, to get a matched register and the amounts to investigate
When one invoice looks wrong, to recalculate every line and total and list missing fields
When there are purchase orders, to match each invoice to its order and code it
When goods were short or wrong, to match order, receipt and invoice and write to the supplier
When the same exceptions return each month, to track new and resolved ones with evidence

tasks.task: Scan for duplicate and double payments

items.when: When a batch may hold the same bill twice under a changed number or date
When you have invoices, approved vendors and your approval rule, to check each for duplicates
When one supplier appears under several spellings, which hides double payments
When you have a long payment history, to flag the odd ones with a reason for each

tasks.task: Plan a supplier payment run that protects cash

items.when: When bills are checked and you must decide who is paid this run from the cash you have
When bills still need reading, coding and matching before a run can be approved
Before approving the run, to see cash at 30, 60 and 90 days with the run included
When cash is tight, to see your float and which suppliers to ask for longer terms

tasks.task: Check a supplier's request to change bank details

items.when: When new bank details arrive by email or on an invoice, before anything is changed or paid
When a payment may already have gone to the wrong account, to trace it and list red flags
When a message presses you to act fast, to check it through a route you already trust

tasks.task: Offer a payment plan to a customer who is struggling

items.when: When a customer cannot pay in full and you would sooner agree a plan than lose them
Before you name figures, to find a range they can pay and a sum they can meet
When you want the offer and a firm follow-up drafted together to compare
Before you send it, to check your own cash can carry the slower payments

tasks.task: Prepare a phone call about an overdue payment

items.when: When emails have not worked and the next step in the plan is a call
Before the call, to get an opening, calm questions and a fallback
When the customer disputes the bill, to have lines ready that lower the heat
When the customer avoids a date, to sum up their side and ask how they would fix it

tasks.task: Set up payment terms and how the business bills

items.when: When late payment is common and terms, deposits and billing dates need to be set
When a customer sends their own contract, to find payment clauses that hurt you
When the terms are agreed, to put them in plain words customers will read

tasks.task: Write a credit application form and credit limit rules

items.when: When you give terms to anyone who asks, or a bad debt has made you nervous
When a customer shares accounts, to judge whether they can pay what they will owe
When a few customers hold most of the debt, to set limits for the biggest
When a limit is set on hope, to look at the downside and leave a margin

tasks.task: Design an invoice and numbering that gets paid

items.when: When invoices bounce back from payables teams or you are setting up invoicing
When one invoice must go out now, with the totals added up and checked
Before it is sent, to recalculate each line and list missing fields or date problems

tasks.task: Write the rules for recurring billing

items.when: When plans or retainers hit awkward cases: a mid-month start, an upgrade, a failed card
When subscribers need billing reminders and confirmations that match the rules
When failed payments lose customers, to plan the recovery steps
After a billing cycle, to check recurring revenue and active subscribers against the rules

tasks.task: Set a billing schedule for a project or retainer

items.when: When a job should be billed in stages with a deposit, not all at the end
When billing depends on time and expenses, to set entry rules, approvals and the handoff
When the schedule is drafted, to see whether it covers costs as they fall due

tasks.task: Tell customers about a change in how you bill

items.when: When you move to deposits, stage payments, shorter terms or e-invoicing
When the change is a price rise, to write a letter that keeps most customers
When the notice reads cold, to try a warmer or plainer version with the same facts
When customers push back, to check each promise in your reply before it goes

tasks.task: Run the weekly money in, money out cycle

items.when: Weekly on fixed days, for example chasing on Tuesday and the payment run on Thursday
When you want the week's chase list and reminders produced from the open invoices
When the week's bills are checked and the run must fit the cash

tasks.task: Close payables and receivables at month end

items.when: In the first three working days after month end, before the books are closed
When the close has no list, to get dated tasks with owners and blockers
When a control account does not agree to its list, to sort the gaps by type
When one difference will not clear, to trace it to the entries on both sides
When bills for the month have not arrived, to draft the accruals with support
Before handing over, to review what does not reconcile and any odd entries

tasks.task: Review aged debt and decide on stops and write-offs

items.when: When the aged report needs an action against every overdue account
When you need rules for putting an account on stop and reopening it
When you want to show how many days of sales sit unpaid and the trend
When a debt is written off or provided for, to draft the entry for the accountant

tasks.task: Reconcile a supplier statement to the ledger

items.when: When you have the statement and the ledger as two tables, to match them and list what is left
When one item differs, to trace it to its source on both sides
When the statement shows an invoice you never received or already paid

tasks.task: Match incoming payments to open invoices

items.when: When you have the bank statement and the ledger, to get matches, near matches and leftovers
When a receipt will not match, to trace what differs
When receipts are matched weekly before the chase list is made, so nobody is chased in error

tasks.task: Handle an invoice dispute or credit request

items.when: First, to check whether the invoice itself is right before you defend it
When you must give a clear yes, partial or no on a credit, from your policy and the facts
When the customer is angry, to draft a reply that names the feeling and fixes what you can
Before sending, to check every promise and the tone, and get a repaired draft

tasks.task: Escalate a debt that reminders have not moved

items.when: When it is time for a formal demand, to build a fact sheet, a timeline and a draft letter
When the debtor is a UK business, to work out the interest and fixed fee to claim
Before legal steps, to offer one last plan as the other road
Before you threaten anything, to read what the contract says on payment and disputes

tasks.task: Write a simple bills-to-payment process

items.when: When the process must say what is checked on every bill and by whom
When the steps from bill received to bill paid need a flowchart and written procedure
When one person runs payables from memory and someone else must be able to cover
When the process trusts one person end to end, to ask how it could be abused

tasks.task: Forecast cash from open invoices and bills

items.when: When you have invoices, bills and fixed costs and need a 30, 60 and 90 day view
When a slow season is coming, to get a dated forecast, a downside case and actions
When last month's forecast missed, to see each miss and why

tasks.task: Find supplier savings and better payment terms

items.when: When you have the vendor bills, to code them, flag odd ones and rank the savings
When you have a list of what was paid, to group spend and find quick wins
When you want to know which terms to ask each supplier for
Each month, to catch renewals and notice dates before they roll over
Before you ask a supplier for longer terms, to plan the opening and a fallback

always.when: Before any message or invoice goes out, to catch typos and names or numbers written two ways
Before any list or schedule is shared, to find broken formulas and totals that do not add up

helpers.when: When postings, bank reconciliation or the ledger itself need fixing before you can chase or pay
When accruals, provisions or month-end reports need an accountant's judgment
When cash is short enough that funding, not chasing, is the real question
When supplier prices, contracts or a tender need work beyond payment terms
When a key account pays late and the relationship needs handling alongside the chase
When the aged report or payment list needs a workbook built or repaired

gaps: No library item writes a phone script for a payment call
No library item checks a supplier's bank-detail change or screens an email for invoice fraud; only the kit prompt does
No library item writes a credit application form or sets credit limits from customer data
No library item offers invoice layouts to compare or sets an invoice numbering scheme
No library item writes recurring billing rules for part months, upgrades and failed cards
No library item builds a billing schedule for a staged project or retainer
No library item reconciles a supplier statement to the payables ledger; only general table matching exists
No library item allocates receipts to invoices with part payments and remittance advices
No library item works out late payment interest or legal steps outside the UK
No library item lists the fields a tax invoice or e-invoice needs in each country
No library item checks a reminder for the right amount, date, invoice number and tone before it is sent
No library item sets approval limits and split duties for a small finance team
No library item sets a bad debt provision from an aged debt report
